Thomas D. Westergaard is a Danish designer and founder of Ceremoni Studio, where he transforms the traditional candle into a kinetic sculpture. Instead of treating wax as a static object, he engineers candles that bend, twist, and weave together as they burn. Every prototype is tested through long time-lapse recordings to study the flame, the melting wax, and the structure, refining each design until movement and combustion become one. His work sits somewhere between industrial design, engineering, and performance. #art #artist #avantgarde #candles #timelapse

Janel Hawkins, founder of Sand Castle University, transforms compacted sand into detailed sculptures, from elaborate castles to animals and imaginative characters. Carving away small sections and smoothing each surface, she gradually turns a simple mound into shapes with surprisingly crisp edges and intricate details. The process is mesmerizing to watch, especially knowing how temporary the finished work is. Each sculpture takes patience and precision, even though the sand will eventually lose its shape. This is the clock that becomes digital from analog a stunning piece of kinetic art and engineering. Dozens of individual analog clocks are arranged in a grid on a large wall panel. Each clock has two independently controlled hands. When the time changes, every hand rotates in perfect coordination so that groups of clocks form the shapes of digital numbers. Six clocks typically work together to create one digit. Across the full wall they display hours and minutes in clear digital form, then smoothly transition to the next minute with a mesmerizing dance of moving hands. #clock #art  #worldrecord

“You Never Have to Smoke Alone” is a kinetic sculpture by Danish-Icelandic artist Jeppe Hein, known for creating interactive works that subtly reshape how viewers experience space. Using motion and air to form drifting, smoke-like shapes, the piece turns something fleeting into a shared visual moment. It emphasizes impermanence, presence, and quiet connection, inviting viewers to slow down and engage with the work as it unfolds in real time. #art #Sculpture ##artist##museum##museums
